#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

strlist.c: wrap 6 items (wave-184/batch-0/run-1)

fn::git_strlist_contains_prefix
fn::git_strlist_copy
fn::git_strlist_copy_with_null
fn::git_strlist_free
fn::git_strlist_free_with_null
fn::git_strlist_contains_key

Waves 184 and 185 in one batch. The copies and releasers are two policies
over libgit2's allocator, StrListFree (git_strlist_copy, git_strlist_free)
and NullStrListFree (git_strlist_copy_with_null, git_strlist_free_with_null),
held by the owners StrList and NullStrList, whose elements are alloc.rs's
AllocStr: each list's array lives in a private CVec of ManuallyDrop<AllocStr>,
its C releaser frees every string and the array, and the lists dereference to
&[AllocStr] / &mut [AllocStr]. Neither policy can be built outside the module,
so its releaser only receives a list's array. The searches are contains_prefix
and contains_key over any run of borrowed strings. C's leak on a refused copy
and contains_key's comparison without the delimiter are kept and documented.

The raw bindings gain strlist.h and the six functions. The ownership store
records the pointer findings of all six; the lifecycle roles planning
submitted (deep cloners of `in`, droppers of `strings`) are confirmed by the
bodies, unchanged. Proposal: crustify/evolution/elementwise-releasers.

Co-Authored-By: crustify <crustify@berkeley.edu>

NULL until the first error. Read by llhttp_get_error_reason (httpclient's git_http_parser_errmsg)."}},
    "error_pos": {"ptr": {"scalar": null, "array": {"by_val": true}, "string": false, "owned": false, "borrowed": {"lifetime": "other"}, "nullable": true, "mutable": false,
      "note": "Points into the `p`..`endp` input of the llhttp_execute call that failed or paused (the generated error and pause states, and llhttp__internal_execute's span error, which stores endp).     "settings": {"ptr": {"scalar": {"by_val": true}, "array": null, "string": false, "owned": false, "borrowed": {"lifetime": "other"}, "nullable": true, "mutable": false,
      "note": "The caller's const llhttp_settings_t, stored by llhttp_init and kept by llhttp_reset; llhttp.h requires it to live at least as long as the parser. api.c's CALLBACK_MAYBE/SPAN_CALLBACK_MAYBE read it as const and call its callbacks; NULL runs none.     "_span_pos0": {"ptr": {"scalar": null, "array": {"by_val": true}, "string": false, "owned": false, "borrowed": {"lifetime": "other"}, "nullable": true, "mutable": false,
      "note": "Start of the open span within the current input; llhttp__internal_execute rebases it to each call's `p` and passes it to _span_cb0 at the call's end. NULL when no span is open. Private to llhttp.c."}},
    "_span_cb0": {"ptr": {"scalar": {"by_val": true}, "array": null, "string": false, "owned": false, "borrowed": {"lifetime": "static"}, "nullable": true, "mutable": false,
      "note": "A function pointer erased to void *: the llhttp__internal__span_cb (llhttp__on_url, ...) of the open span, called by llhttp__internal_execute. Private to llhttp.c."}},
    "_current": {"ptr": {"scalar": {"by_val": true}, "array": null, "string": false, "owned": false, "borrowed": {"lifetime": "static"}, "nullable": true, "mutable": false,
      "note": "Not a pointer to memory: the llparse_state_t of the next state, cast to void * through intptr_t; 0 is s_error. Never dereferenced. Private to llhttp.c."}}
  }

## Legend

- `module` / `wave` / `batch` — the batch's place in `schedule.json`: its wave's module and
  the wave and batch indices
- `objective` — `wrap` or `port`; `pass` — `first` for a translation batch, `review` for a
  review batch; `Σ first` / `Σ review` total each pass apart
- `types` / `symbols` / `fields` — the batch's scheduled units (callbacks count as
  symbols) and its types' assigned field accessors; a review row counts what it reviewed
- `$` / `tokens` / `wall` — the agent's computed cost (API-equivalent under
  subscription), its tokens in millions as `crustify usage` reports them, and its elapsed
  time, C rebuild included; `$/<unit>` divides `$` by the row's units
- `+LoC` — the landing's Rust insertions/deletions; `loc` — its `.rs` insertions
- `cov (C/Rust)` — line coverage after the landing, all test workloads in one run: C over
  the link unit's TUs, Rust over non-test sources; a `Σ` cell is the pass's last landing
- `+UB safe tests` … `+unit tests` — the tests the landing added, with its C/Rust coverage
  change in pp
- `+lifecycle` … `+misc`, `total` — the reports a review batch filed, by kind
- safety audit columns — the Safety audit's metrics, as a landing changed them
- API stability columns — the landing's items by how `ffimap api` classifies their consumer-facing API against its base: `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed`, `new`, and `→Replaces` for the anchors a port moved; `unattributed` the crate's public items no anchor reaches, by module; `reasons` the changed and removed items with the reason the batch recorded
- `cost` / `review cost` / `total` — a module's translation, review and combined cost;
  `module wall` — first launch to final gate; `Σ recorded agents` leaves the assistant
  out, `Σ campaign` adds it, without per-unit cells
- `UB safe tests` … `Unit tests` — `#[test]` functions per suite, each with the coverage of
  running it alone; `Total tests` — all four, whose coverage is one joint run's union,
  never the sum
- `total`, `ported` and `wrapped` types and symbols — the scheduled public-API units, and

## Safety audit

Deterministic `ffimap`, run as the `ffimap` skill's Accounting section describes; no
model. Every counter is in the `ffimap.json` tracked in the campaign's artifact dir, in
each wave's `waves/wave-<index>/` and in each batch run's dir. Each metric is one counter
or a combination of counters, named by their dotted paths into the scan's `counts`; a `%`
metric is a share within one record, and a `−` subtracts a share from the record it cuts.

### Metrics

| metric | counters | what it counts |
|---|---|---|
| pub raw ptr | `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` | raw pointers a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`: public fields and the signatures of safe public fns; target 0 |
| pub void ptr | `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` | type-erased pointers left to the API's users, `unsafe fn`s included |
| pub unsafe fn | `fn.unsafe.pub` | the obligations the crate exports to its callers |
| &cell | `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub` | public references to a cell outside the positions ffibox sanctions, where the convention wants a handle; target 0 |
| C by value | `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total` + `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total` | C structs held by value or in a standard-library owner rather than through a cell, which a move can leave dangling |
| celled % | `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` / `….of_which.used` | of the C types the bindings pass by pointer that the crate uses, those a cell covers |
| raw→std | `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.total` | raw pointers turned into a standard-library borrow, slice, string or owner, whose lifetime or ownership the type system then trusts |
| unmanaged ptr types | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total` | types that store a raw pointer and declare nothing about it |
| ptr Drop | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total` | types that store a raw pointer and free it by hand, rather than through an owner |
| Send/Sync | `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total` + `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total` | thread safety asserted rather than derived from the fields |
| raw deref | `raw_ptr.deref.total` | raw-pointer reads and writes in bodies, each a pointer the code vouches for |
| FFI calls | `code.unsafe_call.ffi` | calls across the C boundary, through bindings or stored function pointers |
| unsafe loc % | `code.loc.unsafe` / `code.loc.total` | lines of unsafe code over code lines; the comparable measure of unsafe volume |
| unsafe blocks | `code.unsafe_block.total` − `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` | hand-written unsafe blocks, a port's generated export gateways left out; moves with the one-op-per-block policy, so not comparable across crates |

## Safety audit

Deterministic `ffimap`, run as the `ffimap` skill's Accounting section describes; no
model. Every counter is in the `ffimap.json` tracked in the campaign's artifact dir, in
each wave's `waves/wave-<index>/` and in each batch run's dir. Each metric is one counter
or a combination of counters, named by their dotted paths into the scan's `counts`; a `%`
metric is a share within one record, and a `−` subtracts a share from the record it cuts.

### Metrics

| metric | counters | what it counts |
|---|---|---|
| pub raw ptr | `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` | raw pointers a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`: public fields and the signatures of safe public fns; target 0 |
| pub void ptr | `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` | type-erased pointers left to the API's users, `unsafe fn`s included |
| pub unsafe fn | `fn.unsafe.pub` | the obligations the crate exports to its callers |
| &cell | `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub` | public references to a cell outside the positions ffibox sanctions, where the convention wants a handle; target 0 |
| C by value | `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total` + `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total` | C structs held by value or in a standard-library owner rather than through a cell, which a move can leave dangling |
| celled % | `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` / `….of_which.used` | of the C types the bindings pass by pointer that the crate uses, those a cell covers |
| raw→std | `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.total` | raw pointers turned into a standard-library borrow, slice, string or owner, whose lifetime or ownership the type system then trusts |
| unmanaged ptr types | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total` | types that store a raw pointer and declare nothing about it |
| ptr Drop | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total` | types that store a raw pointer and free it by hand, rather than through an owner |
| Send/Sync | `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total` + `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total` | thread safety asserted rather than derived from the fields |
| raw deref | `raw_ptr.deref.total` | raw-pointer reads and writes in bodies, each a pointer the code vouches for |
| FFI calls | `code.unsafe_call.ffi` | calls across the C boundary, through bindings or stored function pointers |
| unsafe loc % | `code.loc.unsafe` / `code.loc.total` | lines of unsafe code over code lines; the comparable measure of unsafe volume |
| unsafe blocks | `code.unsafe_block.total` − `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` | hand-written unsafe blocks, a port's generated export gateways left out; moves with the one-op-per-block policy, so not comparable across crates |

#!/bin/bash
# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"

# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"

"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
import subprocess,sys,pathlib,json,glob,os
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'
    subprocess.run([B+'llvm-profdata','merge','-sparse','-o',str(prof)]+raws,check=True)
    return prof
def total(prof,srcs):
    cd=[]
    if srcs==['@c']: use,srcs=cobjs,[]
    else:
        use=objs
        if '@' in srcs[-1]: srcs[-1],c=srcs[-1].split('@'); cd=['-compilation-dir='+c]
    args=[B+'llvm-cov','report','-instr-profile',str(prof)]+cd+[use[0]]+sum((['-object',o] for o in use[1:]),[])+srcs
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.returncode: sys.exit(r.stderr[-2000:])
    lines=r.stdout.splitlines()
    if srcs and not cd:
        roots=[str(pathlib.Path(d).resolve()) for d in srcs]
        rows=[l.split()[0] for l in lines[2:] if l.strip() and not l.startswith(('-','TOTAL','Filename'))]
        stray=[f for f in rows if not any(str(pathlib.Path(f).resolve()).startswith(r+'/') or str(pathlib.Path(f).resolve())==r for r in roots)]
        if stray: sys.exit(f'scope {srcs} reports {len(stray)} files outside it, such as {stray[0]}: its filters match no source')
    t=[l for l in lines if l.startswith('TOTAL')][-1].split()
    # TOTAL regions missed cover functions missed exec lines missed cover branches missed cover
    return dict(lines=(int(t[7])-int(t[8]),int(t[7]),t[9]),functions=(int(t[4])-int(t[5]),int(t[4]),t[6]),regions=(int(t[1])-int(t[2]),int(t[1]),t[3]))
res={}
skip=os.environ.get('MERGED')
four=[x for x in suites if x!='doc']
only=os.environ.get('ONLY')
for s in ([only] if only else suites+['TOTAL','ALL']):
    prof=out/f'{s}.profdata' if skip else merge(s,four if s=='TOTAL' else suites if s=='ALL' else [s])
    res[s]={n:total(prof,src.split(':')) for n,src in scopes.items()}
    print(s,json.dumps(res[s]))
(out/(f'figures-{only}.json' if only else 'figures.json')).write_text(json.dumps(res,indent=1))

1	# Counter schema
2	
3	The counters ffimap reports: what each one holds, how a record is shaped, and
4	how a report is built from them. Every counter is determined from declarations
5	and single expression nodes -- no value is followed, no cast chain is composed,
6	and no dataflow is performed.
7	
8	What each counter is decided FROM, and how a scan runs, is
9	[`analysis.md`](analysis.md); the ffibox vocabulary the `<trait>` and
10	`<primitive>` arms are generated from is [`ffibox.md`](ffibox.md).
11	
12	## 1. The counters
13	
14	Each row below is one counter, named by its dotted path into the document's
15	`counts`. A `{a,b}` is a split the counter carries: `raw_ptr.field.{pub,priv}`
16	is two leaves, and every row's leaves are integers. Each partition also carries
17	a `total`, derived from its children unless the driver emits it, so
18	`raw_ptr.field.total` exists and `raw_ptr.field.pub + raw_ptr.field.priv`
19	equals it; the `of_which` rows are shares of the row above them and are never
20	summed ([2.1](#21-partitions-and-shares)).
21	
22	The counters are the whole of the document's `counts`. There is no second,
23	flat counter block beside them, and no prose rendering of them: a reader who
24	wants a rate divides the leaves it names.
25	
26	Across the tree, `unsafe` and `safe` are the safety of the *function* the
27	position or site is in, `pub` and `priv` whether a consumer of the crate can
28	reach the item, and `void` a pointer whose pointee is erased (`*c_void`). A row
29	naming `ffibox`, a `<trait>` or a `<primitive>` is present only under
30	`--ffibox`, an `of_which.seam` row only with `--seams`, and a `region` or
31	`outside_regions` row only with `--regions`; each is absent rather than zero
32	otherwise ([2.3](#23-zero-and-absent)). A row ends with the property it bears
33	on, as [goals.md](goals.md) names them: safety, soundness, ergonomics or
34	idiomaticity.
35	
36	### 1.1 `raw_ptr`
37	
38	The raw pointers the crate declares in its signatures and types, and what its
39	bodies do with them.
40	
41	- `raw_ptr.total.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the denominator: every
42	  raw-pointer position the crate CHOSE, which is `fn_sig_arg` plus
43	  `fn_sig_ret` plus `field`. Emitted rather than derived, so it is not a sum of
44	  the families beside it ([analysis 9.2](analysis.md#92-what-raw_ptrtotal-admits)).
45	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- raw pointers an argument of
46	  a signature takes. Taking is the hazard: a safe fn that takes one lets a
47	  caller pass anything with no `unsafe` at the call site.
48	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the
49	  erased ones. Subtract the share for the typed ones.
50	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the
51	  ones in a function `--seams` declared to be nothing but a conversion between
52	  a wrapper and its raw pointer.
53	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- raw pointers a signature
54	  returns. Returning one still forces the caller to write `unsafe` before it
55	  means anything, which is why it is counted apart from `fn_sig_arg`.
56	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
57	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
58	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- positions in a trait
59	  impl's method, both directions in one counter: a trait declaration fixed the
60	  signature, so the crate did not choose the position, and the figure would
61	  otherwise move with how many types a trait is implemented for
62	  ([analysis 9.3](analysis.md#93-positions-a-trait-fixed)).
63	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
64	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
65	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.std.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of
66	  those, the ones a standard-library trait fixed.
67	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.local.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the
68	  ones a trait the crate declared itself fixed.
69	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the
70	  ones an ffibox contract fixed, which for a crate built on the convention is
71	  its lifecycle strategies.
72	- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` -- those by
73	  trait, over the whole vocabulary, so a document says which contracts reach a
74	  raw pointer and which do not. No safety or visibility split: a trait method's
75	  are the declaration's ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
76	- `raw_ptr.field.{pub,priv}` -- struct and union fields declared with a raw
77	  pointer. `pub` is one reachability question, the type exported AND the field
78	  exported, rather than two levels a reader has to combine.
79	- `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the erased ones.
80	- `raw_ptr.deref.{rd,wr}` -- dereference sites in bodies, by whether the place
81	  is read or written. Sites, not positions, so they are outside `raw_ptr.total`.
82	- `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{owner,string,borrow,slice,other}` -- a raw pointer
83	  converted into a standard-library shape, by the shape it became: an owner
84	  (`Box`, `Vec`, `Rc`, `Arc`), a string (`CStr`, `CString`, `String`), a
85	  borrow, a slice. `other` is a shape the table does not know, which for `std`
86	  is none of them ([analysis 11.3](analysis.md#113-other)).
87	- `raw_ptr.casted_to.ffibox.{owner,string,borrow,slice}` -- adopted into an
88	  ffibox primitive, by the primitive's group. There is no `other` arm: every
89	  primitive maps to a shape.
90	- `raw_ptr.casted_to.local_seam.{owner,string,borrow,slice,other}` -- converted
91	  through a function `--seams` named, by the seam's return type. `other` is a
92	  seam returning a bespoke handle.
93	- `raw_ptr.surrendered.std.{owner,string}` -- the other direction: a value
94	  Rust owns turned into a raw pointer by a standard-library call, such as
95	  `Box::into_raw` or `CString::into_raw`, by the shape it had. What C is then
96	  trusted to give back to the allocator that made it (soundness).
97	- `raw_ptr.surrendered.ffibox.<shape>` -- the same through an ffibox
98	  primitive's `into_raw`, `into_c` or `into_raw_parts`, by the primitive's
99	  shape, as `casted_to.ffibox` reads it (soundness).
100	
101	### 1.2 `ty`
102	
103	The types the crate defines, by what they hold and what they declare about it.
104	
105	- `ty.total.{pub,priv}` -- every type the crate defines. Emitted, and the
106	  denominator its shares are read against.
107	- `ty.total.of_which.std_trait.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the types that
108	  implement a standard-library trait.
109	- `ty.total.of_which.local_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement a
110	  trait the crate declared itself.
111	- `ty.total.of_which.ffibox_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement an
112	  ffibox contract.
113	- `ty.total.of_which.no_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: types that
114	  implement no trait at all.
115	- `ty.total.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- the types a macro wrote, such as
116	  `bitflags!`'s: subtract for the hand-written ones, as for `fn.total`.
117	- `ty.total.of_which.{repr_c,repr_transparent}.{pub,priv}` -- the types whose
118	  layout is C's (`#[repr(C)]`) or exactly another type's
119	  (`#[repr(transparent)]`): the layouts the crate shares with C (soundness).
120	- `ty.total.of_which.std_impl.<trait>.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement
121	  one of a fixed list of std traits a Rust consumer expects of a value, by
122	  trait: `Debug`, `Display`, `Error`, `Clone`, `Default`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`,
123	  `Hash`, `Iterator` and `From`, derived or written (idiomaticity).
124	- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.{pub,priv}` -- types whose fields reach a raw pointer,
125	  within the peel set, so these are the types that manage one themselves
126	  rather than delegating to `Vec` or to an ffibox owner
127	  ([analysis 9.1](analysis.md#91-the-peel-set)).
128	- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones that
129	  implement `Drop`: they free memory Rust did not allocate.
130	- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that
131	  implement `Clone`, where a shallow clone duplicates the pointer and, with
132	  `Drop`, double-frees it.
133	- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.{impl_deref,impl_deref_mut}.{pub,priv}` -- the
134	  ones that hand out a reference derived from the pointer implicitly, at every
135	  call site.
136	- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_send_sync.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that
137	  assert thread safety for memory no type system checked.
138	- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.has_lifetime.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that tie
139	  the pointer to a lifetime parameter.
140	- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that declare
141	  their lifecycle through an ffibox contract, which none of the std shares can
142	  see.
143	- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.pub_field.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that publish
144	  the pointer as a public field. Not a declaration: an access the type does not
145	  govern.
146	- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: the type
147	  stores a pointer and declares nothing about it, in any vocabulary.
148	- `ty.wrapping_unsafe_cell.{pub,priv}` -- types holding an `UnsafeCell`, the
149	  one way to hold a value C may write while Rust holds a shared reference to it.
150	- `ty.impl_block.{pub,priv}` -- inherent `impl T` blocks: the API the crate
151	  wrote for its own type.
152	- `ty.impl_block.of_which.ffibox.{layout,ref,mut,locked}.{pub,priv}` -- of
153	  those, the blocks on a cell and on each of its handles, which are different
154	  surfaces: the layout type carries the constructors, the shared handle the
155	  getters, the exclusive handle the setters.
156	- `ty.impl_block.of_which.other.{pub,priv}` -- the blocks on everything else.
157	- `ty.impl_trait.{pub,priv}` -- `impl Tr for T` blocks: satisfying someone
158	  else's shape.
159	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.unsafe` -- of those, the `unsafe impl`s, which assert
160	  what the compiler cannot check. `TrivialClone`, which `#[derive(Clone)]`
161	  emits, is skipped.
162	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.derived.{pub,priv}` -- the ones a `#[derive]` wrote.
163	  Nobody typed them, and they are most of the `std` arm.
164	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.drop.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a
165	  standard-library trait, by trait: `Drop`, which runs code when an object is
166	  released.
167	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.clone.{pub,priv}` -- `Clone`, which duplicates
168	  one.
169	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` -- `Send`, the claim that an
170	  object may move to another thread.
171	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}` -- `Sync`, the claim that it may
172	  be shared between threads.
173	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.ref_forming.{pub,priv}` -- `Deref`, `DerefMut`,
174	  `AsRef`, `AsMut`, `Borrow`, `BorrowMut`, `Index` and `IndexMut`, whose
175	  method returns a reference of a type the impl chose.
176	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.other.{pub,priv}` -- every other std trait:
177	  `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Copy` and the rest.
178	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.local.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a trait the crate
179	  declared itself: a shape it chose rather than adopted.
180	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of an ffibox
181	  trait that states a cell's layout or how it is reached and locked: the
182	  layout, seam and guard groups of [ffibox.md](ffibox.md#1-the-vocabulary).
183	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
184	  those by trait, split by whether a generator wrote the impl rather than by
185	  visibility ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
186	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a lifecycle
187	  policy: the allocate, release and clone groups.
188	- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
189	  those by trait, likewise.
190	- `ty.generic.{pub,priv}` -- types carrying a generic parameter.
191	- `ty.generic.of_which.{lifetime,type}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, by kind of
192	  parameter. A lifetime ties the type to something it borrows; a type parameter
193	  makes it a family rather than one layout, so each instantiation is a separate
194	  question about C's bytes. A type may carry both.
195	- `ty.generic.of_which.storing_raw_ptr.{pub,priv}` -- the generic types that
196	  hold a raw pointer.
197	- `ty.field.ffibox.<primitive>.{pub,priv}` -- fields holding an ffibox
198	  primitive, by primitive: the delegation `ty.storing_raw_ptr` deliberately
199	  does not count as the crate's own pointer.
200	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.{pub,priv}` -- the cell types: those that implement
201	  `CCell`.
202	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.no_seam_trait.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the cells
203	  whose handles implement neither seam, so code generic over a handle has to
204	  special-case them.
205	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` -- MENTIONS of a cell in the
206	  crate's declarations, by what holds it: a cell named in twenty signatures is
207	  twenty of these. Here, the mentions behind a reference, which the convention
208	  says should be a handle instead.
209	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- of
210	  those, where they sit: a field's type, or a signature's. These two partition
211	  each arm of `as`.
212	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.{pub,priv}`
213	  -- of the references, the receiver of an `as_ref` / `as_mut` accessor, which
214	  ffibox's contract licenses.
215	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.{pub,priv}` --
216	  the receiver of a trait impl's method, whose shape the trait fixed rather
217	  than the crate. The remainder of the references is the unsanctioned surface.
218	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.of_which.ref_forming.{pub,priv}`
219	  -- of those, the receivers of a `ref_forming` std trait's method, which
220	  returns a reference the impl chose.
221	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions held by an
222	  ffibox borrow: `CBorrowedPtr`, `CSlice`, `CSliceMut`, `CGuardedRef`,
223	  `CGuard`.
224	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` --
225	  where they sit.
226	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.std.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions held by a
227	  standard-library owner of its own storage (`Box`, `Vec`, a map).
228	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- where
229	  they sit.
230	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions held by an
231	  ffibox owner: `CBox`, `CArc`, `CVec`, `CVal`.
232	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` --
233	  where they sit.
234	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.by_val.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions with nothing above
235	  them: the cell's bytes sit in the mention's own place.
236	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.by_val.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- where
237	  they sit.
238	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields.total` -- the crate's fns annotated as accessors
239	  of a C member: each `#[doc(alias = "<root>.<member>{.<member>}")]` whose
240	  member path resolves through the structs and unions the crates
241	  `--sys-crates` names declare, from a struct, a union or a type alias of one,
242	  once per alias and fn, so a getter and a setter of one member are two. The
243	  path names only what has a name: bindgen's `__bindgen_anon_<n>` members are
244	  looked through, a member bindgen escapes with a trailing `_` matches its C
245	  name, a bitfield resolves through the getter bindgen declares for it, and
246	  an array member continues into its element type. Only names are
247	  resolved, never layouts. Fns, not cells, so never summed into
248	  `ty.ffibox.wrapper`, and no `{pub,priv}`, like `ty.ffibox.sys`.
249	- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields.of_which.unique` -- the distinct member paths they
250	  name.
251	- `ty.ffibox.sys.total` -- the structs the crates `--sys-crates` names
252	  declare: the C aggregates the bindings expose. No `{pub,priv}`: they are
253	  another crate's types.
254	- `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.total` -- of those, the ones a `-sys`
255	  declaration puts behind a raw pointer: a function's signature, a field, a
256	  callback typedef's parameters, or a member of a union a pointer reaches.
257	- `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.used` -- of those, the ones
258	  the crate's compiled code names: in a declaration, or as the type of any
259	  expression or binding in a body.
260	- `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` -- of those, the ones
261	  a cell's `CCell::C` names.
262	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` -- the same mentions as
263	  `wrapper.as`'s, of the raw struct a cell covers, its `CCell::C`: the C layout
264	  named where the wrapper could have been.
265	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
266	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.of_which.{self_in_ref_accessor,self_in_trait_impl}.{pub,priv}`
267	  -- as above.
268	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.of_which.ref_forming.{pub,priv}`
269	  -- as above.
270	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
271	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as
272	  above.
273	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
274	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
275	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
276	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
277	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
278	- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
279	
280	### 1.3 `fn`
281	
282	Every function the crate defines, the methods of its trait impls included
283	([analysis 9.4](analysis.md#94-functions-and-methods)).
284	
285	- `fn.total.{pub,priv}` -- the denominator, emitted: every function with a body.
286	- `fn.total.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones a macro wrote.
287	  Subtract for the hand-written total.
288	- `fn.safe.{pub,priv}` -- the safe ones.
289	- `fn.safe.of_which.with_unsafe.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones whose body
290	  contains an `unsafe` block: a safe fn discharging an obligation internally.
291	  Counted on the safe arm only ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
292	- `fn.unsafe.{pub,priv}` -- the `unsafe fn`s. `fn.unsafe.pub` is the unsafe
293	  surface a consumer meets.
294	- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.std.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the methods
295	  of a trait impl, whose `unsafe` the trait's declaration fixed and the impl
296	  cannot drop: here, a standard-library trait's.
297	- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.local.{pub,priv}` -- a trait the crate
298	  declared itself, which put the `unsafe` there one level up.
299	- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- an ffibox contract,
300	  such as `CDrop::c_drop`.
301	- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.other.{pub,priv}` -- any other crate's
302	  trait.
303	- `fn.unsafe.of_which.seam.{pub,priv}` -- the `unsafe fn`s `--seams` names,
304	  which adopt a raw pointer by design. A seam may also be a trait's method, so
305	  this overlaps `in_trait_impl`.
306	- `fn.unsafe.of_which.other.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: neither a trait
307	  impl's method nor a seam, the `unsafe` the crate chose with nothing
308	  requiring it.
309	- `fn.unsafe.of_which.outside_regions.{pub,priv}` -- the `unsafe fn`s outside
310	  every module `--regions` named: the unsafe API the crate did not confine
311	  (safety).
312	- `fn.extern_abi.{pub,priv}` -- the fns the crate defines with a foreign ABI
313	  (`extern "C"`), which C reaches by symbol or by fn pointer (soundness).
314	- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.exported.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones carrying a
315	  C symbol name (`#[no_mangle]`, `#[export_name]`).
316	- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- the ones a macro wrote.
317	- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.catches_unwind.{pub,priv}` -- the ones whose body
318	  calls `std::panic::catch_unwind`, a fn `--barriers` named, or, under
319	  `--ffibox`, ffibox's `callback::barrier`: a panic stopped before it unwinds
320	  into C. The rest is read by subtracting (soundness).
321	- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.raw_ptr_sig.{pub,priv}` -- the ones whose signature
322	  holds a raw pointer.
323	- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.ffibox_sig.{pub,priv}` -- the ones whose signature
324	  holds an ffibox primitive, an owner or handle in place of a pointer.
325	- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.ffibox_macro.{pub,priv}` -- the ones an ffibox macro
326	  wrote, such as its `export_*!` lifecycle exports.
327	- `fn.sig.of_which.c_type.{arg,ret}.{pub,priv}` -- mentions of C's types in
328	  the signatures the crate chose, a trait impl's methods left out: C's scalar
329	  names (`c_int`, `c_char`, and `libc`'s), read from the signature as written
330	  since typeck erases them, and foreign-ABI fn pointers. What a consumer of a
331	  Rust API handles in C's terms (ergonomics).
332	- `fn.sig.of_which.result.ret.{pub,priv}` -- the fns, trait impls' methods
333	  left out, that return a `Result`: failure in Rust's vocabulary rather than
334	  C's status codes (idiomaticity).
335	- `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox.{arg,ret}.<primitive>.{pub,priv}` -- mentions of an
336	  ffibox primitive in a signature, by position and by primitive, the ones
337	  inside a `Result`, an `Option` or a reference included
338	  ([analysis 9.4](analysis.md#94-functions-and-methods)): whether the
339	  vocabulary actually crosses the interface.
340	- `fn.ffibox.sys.total` -- the fns the crates `--sys-crates` names declare:
341	  the C functions the bindings expose, macro shims included. No `{pub,priv}`:
342	  they are another crate's.
343	- `fn.ffibox.sys.of_which.used` -- of those, the ones the crate's compiled code
344	  names, by calling one or coercing it to a pointer.
345	- `fn.ffibox.wrapper.{non_trait,other_trait}` -- the crate's fns annotated as
346	  wrappers of a C function: each `#[doc(alias)]` naming a fn of the `-sys`
347	  crates, once per alias and fn, so the variants a C function is forked into
348	  count once each. By where the annotated fn sits: a free fn or an inherent
349	  method (`non_trait`), or the method of a trait that is no ffibox policy
350	  (`other_trait`). No `{pub,priv}`, like `fn.ffibox.sys`.
351	- `fn.ffibox.wrapper.policy.<trait>` -- the method of an ffibox lifecycle
352	  policy, such as `CDrop::c_drop`, by trait: the allocate, release and clone
353	  groups of [ffibox.md](ffibox.md#1-the-vocabulary).
354	- `fn.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.unique` -- the distinct C functions they name.
355	
356	### 1.4 `static`
357	
358	The statics the crate defines; an `extern` block's declarations are C's.
359	
360	- `static.total.{pub,priv}` -- every static the crate defines. Emitted, and the
361	  denominator its shares are read against.
362	- `static.of_which.mut.{pub,priv}` -- the `static mut`s: shared mutable state
363	  no borrow checks (soundness).
364	- `static.of_which.exported.{pub,priv}` -- the ones carrying a C symbol name,
365	  which C reads by that name (soundness).
366	
367	### 1.5 `code`
368	
369	The size of the crate and what its bodies do, as the denominators the rest is
370	read against.
371	
372	- `code.loc.total` -- lines of code, from the compiled crate: the union of HIR
373	  definition spans, blanks and comments excluded, so items `cfg` removed are
374	  not in the denominator.
375	- `code.loc.unsafe` -- of those, the lines inside an `unsafe` block, filtered
376	  the same way so the two are comparable.
377	- `code.unsafe_block.total` -- `unsafe` blocks, however many lines each holds.
378	- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` -- of those, the ones inside a fn
379	  that is the C-ABI boundary: one with a foreign ABI or a C symbol name, or a
380	  closure inside one ([analysis 9.7](analysis.md#97-regions-and-the-c-abi-boundary)).
381	- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.region.<region>` -- the ones inside a module
382	  `--regions` named, or a module nested in one, by the innermost such module's
383	  name (safety).
384	- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.outside_regions` -- the ones inside none, another
385	  crate's macro expansions included: the unsafe the crate did not confine
386	  (safety).
387	- `code.unsafe_call.ffi` -- unsafe calls whose callee carries a foreign ABI:
388	  the real crossings, counted by the callee's type rather than by its
389	  declaration site, so calls through a stored function pointer are in
390	  ([analysis 10](analysis.md#10-calls)).
391	- `code.unsafe_call.rust` -- unsafe calls to a Rust-ABI function, the crate's
392	  own `unsafe fn`s and the standard library's unsafe constructors alike.
393	- `code.unsafe_call.intrinsic` -- unsafe calls to a compiler intrinsic,
394	  `transmute` among them.
395	- `code.fn_ptr.extern_abi.{local,foreign,other}` -- a fn with a foreign ABI
396	  turned into a fn pointer, by coercion or an `as` cast: how C is handed a
397	  callback. By what the fn is: one the crate defines (`local`), a C fn an
398	  `extern` block declares (`foreign`), or another crate's (`other`)
399	  (soundness).
400	- `code.fn_ptr.extern_abi.ffibox` -- under `--ffibox`, the calls that hand C an
401	  ffibox trampoline or release routine as a fn pointer (`trampoline`,
402	  `release_fn`, `release_fn_of`).
403	- `code.call.ffibox.{status,barrier}` -- under `--ffibox`, the calls to ffibox's
404	  status conventions, which turn a C status into a `Result`, and to its panic
405	  barrier. Read against `code.unsafe_call.ffi` (idiomaticity, soundness).
406	- `code.tests.loc.{total,unsafe}` -- the same two line counts for the test
407	  code, which no other counter includes
408	  ([analysis 9.6](analysis.md#96-test-code)).
409	- `code.tests.unsafe_block` -- `unsafe` blocks in the test code.
410	- `code.tests.fn` -- functions in the test code, including one generated
411	  harness `main` per test binary.
412	
413	## 2. The shape of a record
414	
415	### 2.1 Partitions and shares
416	
417	A partition's children are disjoint and sum to it; an `of_which` node's
418	children are subsets that overlap and are never summed. `nest_ptr` derives
419	every partition `total` bottom-up and skips `of_which` when summing, so no sum
420	is written by the driver and none can disagree with its parts.
421	
422	`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which` is a share family: a type may implement both
423	`Drop` and `Clone`, so its arms overlap and only the record itself is a
424	population. An `of_which` node therefore carries no `total` of its own --
425	summing two shares is not a quantity -- while each share keeps the total of its
426	own `{pub,priv}` partition. A share may refine another share, and then it nests
427	under it: `fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` is the ffibox
428	positions by trait.
429	
430	One child is of another unit: `as` holds the mentions of the types its parent
431	counts -- `ty.ffibox.wrapper` is the cell types, `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as` the
432	places they are named -- so it is never summed into the parent either, while
433	it is a record with a total of its own, which its arms partition. So is
434	`ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields`, the fns annotated as field accessors on those
435	cells.
436	
437	Where a residual is wanted it is emitted as a share named for it --
438	`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none`, `ty.total.of_which.no_trait` -- rather than
439	left for a reader to subtract.
440	
441	### 2.2 Namespaces
442	
443	Three kinds of node carry no derived `total`: an `of_which` node, as above; a
444	node that already carries an emitted one, which is how the denominators
445	`raw_ptr.total`, `ty.total` and `code.loc.total` survive a derivation that
446	would otherwise take their name; and a NAMESPACE, a node whose children are
447	families rather than the parts of one quantity.
448	
449	A top-level prefix is always a namespace -- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg` counts
450	signature positions and `raw_ptr.deref` counts body sites, so their sum means
451	nothing -- and four are namespaces a level down. `ty.ffibox` holds two type
452	counts, the cells (`wrapper`) and the `-sys` crates' types (`sys`), each with
453	its mentions under `as`. `code.tests` holds four separate
454	measurements of the test build: its lines, its unsafe lines -- a subset of them
455	-- its unsafe blocks and its fns; their sum read 103840 on libgit2-bindings, a
456	figure with no unit at all. `fn.sig` holds what a signature carries, in
457	mentions -- a fn taking two `CBox` is two of them -- so it is a share of no
458	count of fns, and `fn.total` beside it is the denominator a reader divides by.
459	Its own arms do carry totals: `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox` is `arg` plus `ret`,
460	which are disjoint. `fn.ffibox` holds two fn counts as `ty.ffibox` holds two
461	type counts: the crate's annotated wrappers (`wrapper`) and the `-sys` crates'
462	fns (`sys`).
463	
464	`nest_ptr` declares them in `NAMESPACES` rather than inferring them, since no
465	shape distinguishes a namespace from a partition: `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg`'s
466	`{safe,unsafe}` children are records with their own totals too, and summing
467	those is exactly right.
468	
469	### 2.3 Zero, and absent
470	
471	Every counter the invocation's flags turn on is in the document, at `0` when
472	it never fired. A reader of one document cannot tell an absent counter from
473	one the schema does not have -- no `owned.std` under `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as`
474	could mean "no cell is held in a std collection" or "that arm was never
475	written" --
476	and the schema is too long to hold in the head, so the driver registers every
477	path it can emit before the passes run and they count up from there.
478	
479	What is absent is what the flags did not turn on, which is a different
480	statement and a deliberate one: the ffibox arms without `--ffibox`, and the
481	`of_which.seam` shares without `--seams`. A `0` there would say the scan
482	looked and found none, when it did not look.
483	
484	The registry is in the driver, beside the passes, and it iterates the same
485	vocabulary lists they do, so the trait and primitive arms cannot drift from
486	it. `RegistryTests` reads the registry off a scan of
487	`tests/fixtures/empty/` -- a crate with nothing in it, whose every counter is
488	therefore 0 -- and holds the other fixtures' fired counters to it.
489	
490	### 2.4 The order of a record
491	
492	A record's children are written in a declared order, most salient first: the
493	record's own `total`, then the splits it is cut by (`unsafe` before `safe`,
494	`pub` before `priv`), then its families, then its shares and arms, and
495	`of_which` last, since a share is read against the partition it cuts across.
496	The prefixes come in this document's order: `raw_ptr`, `ty`, `fn`, `code`.
497	
498	The driver emits a sorted map, so the alternative is alphabetical: `fn` would
499	read `{safe, sig, total, unsafe}`, with the denominator in the middle.
500	
501	A name the order does not hold comes after every name it does, alphabetically.
502	That is where the primitive arms land -- `CArc`, `CBorrowedPtr`, `CBox` -- so a
503	primitive added to ffibox needs no change to the order and still reads
504	predictably. The trait arms are declared, in the order
505	[`ffibox.md`](ffibox.md) gives the vocabulary, so a breakdown by trait reads as
506	the lifecycle it describes rather than alphabetically.
507	`measure.KEY_ORDER` is one table for every level, since a name that earns an
508	early rank in one record earns it in the others: `unsafe` is early as
509	`fn.unsafe`, as `code.loc.unsafe` and as the unsafe trait impls. `fn` is the
510	one name it cannot place for every record, being a prefix as well as one of
511	`code.tests`'s measurements, so it is ranked for the latter. A type count's
512	`as` comes after its `of_which`, since the mentions are read once the types
513	are.
514	
515	### 2.5 Deliberate asymmetries
516	
517	A split that is not carried where a reader might expect it, and why.
518	
519	`ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.{layout,policy}.of_which.<trait>` splits
520	`{handwritten,macro}` but not `{pub,priv}`: whether a generator was used does
521	not vary with visibility, and the split would cost a cell per trait for
522	nothing.
523	
524	`raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` splits by neither:
525	a trait method's safety and visibility are the trait declaration's, one
526	spelling dictating every impl, so the split would restate the parent cell by
527	cell. The parent `ffibox` arm carries both, since the mix of traits a crate
528	implements does move them.
529	
530	`fn.safe.of_which.with_unsafe` is counted on the safe arm only. With
531	`unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` denied, every `unsafe fn` doing anything raw has a
532	block by construction, so counting it there would measure the lint.
533	
534	`raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl` carries no direction, while `fn_sig_arg` and
535	`fn_sig_ret` are separate counters: the direction says what the crate chose to
536	do with the pointer, and in a trait impl it chose neither.
537	
538	## 3. Building a report
539	
540	A report is leaves divided and subtracted, named by their paths. Three rules
541	make the arithmetic sound:
542	
543	- a partition may be summed, an `of_which` may not, and an `as` never with the
544	  types above it. Two shares of one record overlap, so
545	  `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop + impl_clone` is not a quantity, while
546	  `pub + priv` is the record;
547	- a rate stays inside one record, or between a record and the denominator
548	  emitted for it: `fn.unsafe.pub / fn.total.pub`, `code.loc.unsafe /
549	  code.loc.total`, `ty.storing_raw_ptr.pub / ty.total.pub`. Dividing across
550	  prefixes mixes grains -- signature positions by lines of code says nothing;
551	- a share is read against the record it cuts, and the remainder is a
552	  subtraction: `wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` less its two sanctioned shares is
553	  the convention's unsanctioned surface.
554	
555	### 3.1 The readings worth taking
556	
557	Each reading below names the leaves it is made of. The figures are not here: a
558	reading of one crate is in [`analysis.md`](analysis.md), where it is the
559	evidence for a rule, and a reading of several is in
560	[`examples/README.md`](../examples/README.md), where three real documents are
561	tabulated side by side. A figure copied into this document would be a second
562	copy to keep current, and the counters are what this document is for.
563	
564	**How much of the bindings has a cell.** Under `--ffibox` with the `-sys`
565	crates named, `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` against
566	`raw_ptr_in_sys` is the share of the C types the bindings hand around by pointer
567	that the crate has given a cell, and `used` against it the share the crate
568	touches at all, so the gap between the two shares is the C it touches
569	without a cell ([ffibox.md](ffibox.md#8-where-the-declarations-mention-a-cell)). Against `ty.ffibox.sys.total` it reads low by
570	construction, since a by-value struct needs no cell.
571	
572	**How much of the C functions has a wrapper.** Under `--ffibox` with the
573	`-sys` crates named, `fn.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.unique` against
574	`fn.ffibox.sys.total` is the share of the C functions the bindings declare
575	that the crate annotates a wrapper for, and `fn.ffibox.sys.of_which.used`
576	against it the share it calls at all. The annotation is the only record of
577	what a wrapper wraps, so an unannotated wrapper reads as none; the alias is
578	the one the Crustify conventions require. `fn.ffibox.wrapper.total` against
579	`unique` is how many variants a wrapped function was forked into on average.
580	
581	**Which `unsafe fn`s nothing required.** `fn.unsafe.of_which.other` is the
582	unsafe surface the crate chose: no trait declared the method unsafe and no
583	seam adopts a pointer through it. Read it against `fn.unsafe`, and its `pub`
584	leaf against `fn.unsafe.pub`, rather than subtracting `in_trait_impl` and
585	`seam`, which overlap.
586	
587	**What a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`.**
588	`raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` is the raw pointers on the safe public interface,
589	`fn.unsafe.pub` against `fn.total.pub` the public unsafe surface, and
590	`raw_ptr.field.pub` the pointers a public field hands over with no `unsafe` at
591	all.
592	
593	**How much unsafe, and where it sits.** `code.loc.unsafe / code.loc.total` is
594	the density and `code.unsafe_block.total` the number of blocks; read both,
595	since folding small blocks into large ones moves one and not the other.
596	`code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` subtracts the gateways a port campaign
597	generated, and the `code.unsafe_call` arms say what the unsafe is for: `ffi`
598	is the boundary, `rust` is the standard library's constructors and the crate's
599	own helpers, `intrinsic` is `transmute` and its siblings.
600	
601	**What the crate wrote, as opposed to what a macro did.** Subtract
602	`fn.total.of_which.macro` from `fn.total`, and
603	`ty.impl_trait.of_which.derived` from `ty.impl_trait`. A comparison of two
604	crates without those shares is partly a comparison of how much boilerplate
605	each spells.
606	
607	**What the crate declares about the pointers it manages.**
608	`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none` against `ty.storing_raw_ptr` is the types
609	that hold a pointer and say nothing about it. The other shares say what the
610	rest declared -- `impl_drop`, `impl_clone`, `ffibox` -- and `pub_field` is the
611	opposite of a declaration.
612	
613	**Whether a convention is kept.** Under `--ffibox`,
614	`ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std` less `self_in_ref_accessor` and
615	`self_in_trait_impl` is the bare `&Foo` surface the convention says should be a
616	handle. `as.owned.std` and `as.by_val` against `as.owned.ffibox` say how much
617	of a cell's storage the crate holds itself rather than through ffibox's
618	owners. `ty.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.no_seam_trait` is the cells a generic
619	handle has to special-case, and `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox` whether the
620	vocabulary reaches the interface at all.
621	
622	**What the trait impls do.** `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std`'s arms say which of
623	the crate's adopted traits act on what it wraps: `drop` and `clone` run its
624	lifecycle, `send` and `sync` are claims about threads, `ref_forming` can hand
625	out a reference to it. Under `--ffibox`, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox`'s
626	`layout` and `policy` say how much of the convention is the cells' layout and
627	how much their lifecycle.
628	
629	**Whose shape the pointers in trait impls are.** `fn_sig_trait_impl` is read
630	through its `of_which` arms, never bare: one crate's are a convention's
631	lifecycle strategies, another's its own private helpers, a third's one local
632	conversion trait, and the bare figure is the same for all three.
633	
634	**The test code, beside the library and never added to it.**
635	`code.tests.loc.total` against `code.loc.total` is how much of the tree is
636	tests, and the `code.tests` arms are the only counters that include them.
637	
638	A report of several crates is a table of leaves, one row per crate, with the
639	denominator beside every share.
640	
641	### 3.2 What a comparison requires
642	
643	The document is a pure function of the source tree under a fixed scanner, so
644	two figures are comparable only when the scanner and the flags match: the
645	ffimap commit, the toolchain, `--sys-crates` (which decides what
646	`ty.storing_raw_ptr` admits), `--seams` (which decides what the `seam` shares
647	and `casted_to.local_seam` can see) and any framework the crate is built on.
648	The `scanner` and `sys_crates` fields carry all of it, which is why they are in
649	the document rather than beside it
650	([analysis 1](analysis.md#1-determinism-and-what-it-rests-on)).
651	
652	A counter added or a rule corrected moves figures too. The ones already known
653	to be incomparable across versions are named in
654	[analysis 12](analysis.md#12-what-the-analysis-cannot-see).
655	
656	### 3.3 No target values
657	
658	ffimap has none, and this is the place that says so. Absolute counts are not
659	comparable across crates of different size, and lower is not automatically
660	better: a wrapper over C must contain unsafe, and folding 600 small audited
661	blocks into 200 large ones improves the number while making the crate worse.
662	A reader who wants a rate divides the leaves it names.
663	
664	Finding what is worth looking at is the opposite kind of work, and belongs to
665	a reviewer who reads the code, forms suspicions and defends them. `none` and
666	`no_seam_trait` name an absence, not a defect.
667
